maximum_sharpe_ratio_portfolio.text: `minimum_variance_portfolio` asks "which weights give the lowest possible portfolio variance?", while `maximum_sharpe_ratio_portfolio` asks "which weights give the best risk-adjusted return?" The first needs only `cov_matrix`, because it minimises `w'Σw` with weights summing to 1 and ignores expected returns. The second also requires `mean_returns`, and it uses `risk_free` to maximise the annualised Sharpe ratio. In `minimum_variance_portfolio`, `mean_returns` and `risk_free` are optional and only used to report a Sharpe ratio, so they don't change the weights. Both functions bound weights to [0, 1] unless `allow_short` is set to true.

explain.text: `minimum_variance_portfolio` (Minimum Variance Portfolio) finds the global minimum-variance portfolio: the set of weights that minimises portfolio variance `w'Σw` given your `cov_matrix`, with weights summing to 1. If you set `allow_short` to true, it uses the closed-form solution `Σ⁻¹1 / (1'Σ⁻¹1)`. Otherwise, weights are bounded between 0 and 1 and it solves numerically with SLSQP. You can also pass `mean_returns`, plus `risk_free` and `periods_per_year`, to have a Sharpe ratio reported alongside the weights.

when.text:
`minimum_variance_portfolio` (Minimum Variance Portfolio) fits when your goal is the lowest-risk mix of assets, not the highest return.

- You want the global minimum-variance portfolio: weights that minimise portfolio variance and sum to 1, using only a covariance matrix (`cov_matrix`) and no return forecasts.
- You distrust expected-return estimates and prefer to rely on risk inputs alone. `mean_returns` is optional and only used to report a Sharpe ratio.
- You need either a long-only result (the default, with weights bounded between 0 and 1) or one that permits shorting via `allow_short`, which uses a closed-form solution.
- You want a low-risk baseline to compare other allocation approaches against.
- If you instead want the tangency portfolio, `maximum_sharpe_ratio_portfolio` is listed as the maximum Sharpe ratio (tangency) portfolio.
